note: Work: the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) Act, No. 2 of 2021 (certified 18 January 2021) redefines a 'child' in section 34 of the principal Act (No. 47 of 1956) as a person under sixteen, raises the ages in section 9 from fifteen to sixteen and repeals section 10; the Shop and Office Employees (Amendment) Act, No. 1 of 2021, likewise moves fourteen to sixteen. The principal Act's bar on employing a child (section 13) wasn't read in its own text, so 16 as the general minimum is my reading of the amendment; the 1956 Act's exceptions (family agricultural work, and any for entertainment under the Children and Young Persons Ordinance) weren't read, and the form holds performers barred below 16 (my reading, to check). A 2026 amending bill (Bill 44 of 2026, found by search) may change section 7: it was passed as Act No. 21 of 2026 (certified 8 September 2026), which raises the fines in sections 7(3), 13(2) and 20A(3) from ten thousand rupees to one hundred thousand and changes no age. Read from LankaLAW's compilation of the 2021 Acts (documents.gov.lk, the Government Printer, returned 404 for the Act's URL), and on 2026-11-03 in the Government Printer's own copy (documents.gov.lk, moved to a new address), ss. 4, 5 and 7 in the same words. The principal Act's section 13 and its entertainment exceptions are still unread, so the figures stay secondary. Majority: the Age of Majority Ordinance wasn't found; left null. Service: no conscription law was found; left null.
